q: 181. The approximate loss of pre stress due to creep in steel in pre stressed concrete is about
explain: As per typical prestress loss values referenced in this text, loss due to relaxation/creep of steel is about 3%.

q: 182. The approximate loss of pre stress due to creep in concrete in pre stressed concrete is about
explain: Creep of concrete under sustained prestress causes a loss of about 6% in the initial prestressing force, as per the values used in this text.

q: 183. The approximate loss of pre stress due shrinkage of concrete in pre stressed concrete is about
explain: Shrinkage of concrete leads to a shortening of the member and a corresponding loss of prestress, approximately 3% as per this text.

q: 184. The approximate loss of pre stress pre-tensioned concrete beam is about
explain: Total combined losses (elastic shortening, creep, shrinkage, relaxation) in pre-tensioned concrete beams are typically higher, in the range of 20 to 25%.

q: 185. The approximate loss of pre-stress post tensioned concrete beam is about
explain: Total prestress losses in post-tensioned members are generally somewhat lower than in pre-tensioned members, falling in the range of about 15 to 20%.

q: 186. Normally pre stressing wires are arranged in the
explain: Prestressing tendons/wires are usually placed near the bottom (tension) zone of the beam to counteract the tensile stresses caused by service loads.

q: 187. Most common method of pre stressing used for factory product in is
explain: The long line method, where multiple units are cast and tensioned along a long prestressing bed simultaneously, is the most common technique used in factory precast production.

q: 188. Which of the following losses of pre stress occurs only in pre tensioning and not in post tensioning
explain: In pre-tensioning, the tendons are stressed and anchored before the concrete is cast, so elastic shortening of concrete transfers directly as an additional loss unique to this method, unlike post-tensioning.

q: 189. Pre stress loss due to friction occurs
explain: Friction losses occur due to contact between the tendon and the duct wall/curvature during the stressing operation, which is a feature specific to post-tensioned construction.

q: 190. Which of the following has high tensile strength?
explain: Cold drawn wires undergo strain hardening during the drawing process, giving them significantly higher tensile strength than plain hot rolled wires.

q: 191. High carbon content in steel causes
options: decrease in tensile strength but increase in ductility
increase in tensile strength but decrease in ductility
decrease in tensile strength and ductility
increase in tensile strength and ductility
explain: Higher carbon content in steel increases its hardness and tensile strength but reduces its ductility, making it more brittle.

q: 192. Cube strength of controlled concrete to be used for pre tensioned and post tensioned w respectively should not be less than
explain: As per the specifications referenced in this text, the minimum cube strength required is 42 MPa for pre-tensioned work and 35 MPa for post-tensioned work.

q: 193. Vicat's apparatus is used for
explain: The Vicat apparatus (with the standard plunger) is primarily used to determine the standard/normal consistency of cement paste.

q: 194. The diameter of the vicat plunger is 10 mm and its length varies from
explain: As per IS specifications, the Vicat plunger, 10 mm in diameter, has a length that varies within the range of about 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 195. Soundness test of cement by Le-Chatelier's apparatus gives unsoundness due to
explain: The Le Chatelier soundness test primarily detects unsoundness caused by excess free (uncombined) lime in the cement.

q: 196. Maximum permissible limit of magnesia content in OPC is
explain: As per IS 269 specifications, the maximum permissible magnesium oxide (magnesia) content in OPC is limited to 6%.

q: 197. According to Indian standards, the pozzolana content in Portland pozzolana cement is
explain: As per IS 1489, the pozzolana content permitted in Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) ranges from 10% to 25% by mass.

q: 198. For a constant water cement ratio, decrease in aggregate cement ratio causes
explain: Reducing the aggregate-cement ratio (i.e., using proportionally more cement paste relative to aggregate) at a fixed water-cement ratio increases the paste content available to lubricate the mix, thereby increasing workability.

q: 199. The value of vee bee time for low workability as per IS is prescribed as
explain: As per IS classification, low workability concrete corresponds to a Vee-Bee time of about 10 to 20 seconds.

q: 200. If the compacting factor of concrete is 0.90, then the workability according to IS is
explain: As per the IS classification table used in this text, a compacting factor of 0.90 falls in the 'low' workability category.

q: 201. Minimum water cement ratio required for full hydration of cement is
explain: Theoretically, complete hydration of cement requires a water-cement ratio of about 0.23-0.25, but the practically required minimum accounting for gel-water space is about 0.36, as given in this text.

q: 202. The IS recommend the use of calcium chloride as accelerating admixture in
explain: Calcium chloride, being corrosive to embedded steel, is recommended by IS only for plain (unreinforced) concrete and reinforced concrete under controlled conditions — not for prestressed concrete, where corrosion risk to tendons is critical.

q: 203. In the manufacture of pozzolana cement, the amount of pozzolana material added to ordinary Portland cement clinker is about
explain: As given in this text, about 30% pozzolanic material is blended with OPC clinker in the manufacture of pozzolana cement.

q: 204. The degree of grinding of cement is called
explain: Fineness of cement refers directly to the degree to which the clinker has been ground into fine powder.

q: 205. The hardening is the phenomenon by virtue of which
options: the cement doesn't undergo large change in volume when treated with water
the plastic cement paste changes into hard mass
the cement paste sets and develops strength
explain: Hardening specifically refers to the process by which the plastic cement paste, after setting, transforms into a hard, rigid mass over time.

q: 206. The phenomenon by virtue of which the cement doesn't undergo large change in volume when treated with water is known as
explain: Soundness is defined as the property of cement to not undergo significant volume change (expansion) after setting when reacted with water.

q: 207. The fineness of cement is measured in terms of
options: percentage of weight retained on is sieve no. 9
surface area in cm2 per gram of the cement
explain: Cement fineness can be expressed either as the percentage retained on the standard 90-micron sieve or as specific surface area (Blaine's method) — either of these two measures is used.

q: 208. Too much fineness of cement
explain: Very fine cement hydrates faster, generating more heat of hydration, which can lead to thermal cracking in concrete — so both effects (a and b) occur.

q: 209. To prevent segregation, the maximum height for placing concrete is
explain: As per good practice referenced in this text, concrete should not be dropped or placed from a height exceeding about 150 cm to prevent segregation.

q: 210. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known as
explain: Curing is the process of maintaining adequate moisture and temperature conditions in freshly placed concrete to allow proper hydration and strength development.

q: 211. Curing of pavements, floors, roofs and slabs is done by
explain: For flat horizontal surfaces such as pavements, floors, roofs, and slabs, the ponding method (retaining a layer of water on the surface using small embankments) is a common and effective curing technique.

q: 212. While compacting the concrete by mechanical vibrator, slump should not exceed
explain: For mechanically vibrated concrete, the recommended slump should not exceed about 50 mm, since higher slump/wetter mixes are meant for hand compaction.

q: 213. Ultimate strength of cold drawn high steel wires
options: increases with increase in diameter of bar
decreases with increase in diameter of bar
doesn't depend on diameter of bar
explain: Due to the reduced degree of cold working achievable in thicker sections, the ultimate tensile strength of cold drawn high-tensile steel wires decreases as the wire diameter increases.

q: 214. Pre-stressing losses in post tensioned and pre tensioned beams are respectively
explain: As per the values used in this text, the overall prestress loss is about 15% for post-tensioned beams and 20% for pre-tensioned beams.

q: 215. In concrete, use of angular crushed aggregate in place of natural rounded gravel affects
explain: Angular crushed aggregate provides better mechanical interlock and bond with the cement matrix, which particularly improves the flexural tensile strength of the concrete.

q: 216. Endurance limit of mild steel is approximately equal to
explain: The endurance (fatigue) limit of mild steel is approximately 0.5 times its ultimate tensile strength.

q: 217. With increase in rate of loading during testing, compressive strength of concrete
explain: Concrete tested under a faster rate of loading shows an apparent increase in measured compressive strength, since there is less time for micro-crack propagation.

q: 218. For a given aggregate content, increasing the water cement ratio in concrete
explain: Note: while a higher water-cement ratio typically increases drying shrinkage in practice, per the book's listed answer, for a given (fixed) aggregate content increasing the water-cement ratio is stated to decrease shrinkage.

q: 219. The bond strength between steel and concrete is due to
explain: Bond between steel reinforcement and concrete develops from a combination of chemical adhesion, frictional resistance, and mechanical interlock — both friction and adhesion contribute.

q: 220. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement cube after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS 269 specifications, the minimum 7-day compressive strength requirement for OPC mortar cubes is 17.5 N/mm².
